questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Studying the language and culture where they speak it. Being able to live and explore the people of the history I have studied.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not know what to expect when going abroad to study, but in many ways I was overwhelmed. The level of difficulty on the courses was high, and there were taken no precautions to being an erasmus as we were judged like one of the spanish student. While this is considered good as all is equal it´s simply not fair for a forener to be judged on a language they are having as a third language the same way as someone native. I had used duble the time to read on homework and other essays and try to figure out their system only to try and keep up with the students who have tried nothing else. At least for me who only had subjects in spanish philology and humanities I found it difficult to keep up with the level of memorising and no use of even a dictionary under the exams. If I could have brought some notes or a dictionary I might have done a lot better to my exams.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not even easy to find the international office, but when I finally found it the staff were nice and tried their best to help. I had missed the "automatriculación" and did therefore not have a schedule which made the beginning of the semester extra difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got some emails from the university and there was the option to participate in welcome days 2 days before official start, where we were properly introduced to the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Used the app "idealista" which had a ton of offers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The busses from and to the university are always cramped. If you live in the city center there is more space in the bus as the route starts here, bit when we arrived at the popular beach area was the bus to full to take in more students making them have to wait for the next. I did not know you could live on campus, but Im satisfied with where I spend my exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a broad selection of places rating at different prices and number of roommates so you could find something that you could be satisfied with.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it too late. They had a deadline to register in one week in the middle of summerbreak which I was not checking my university e-mail. Afterwards the process of registration became irritating and long. had to wait 1 week at a time for an answer to my application and the process was not completed until the first of november, when I only had about 1 month of lectures left before the exams.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They try to inform with speeches and meetings where you get all information and can ask additionally. They will answer your mail but it might take them a week to respond. My first application got lost initially and they had declined it having afterwards realised their mistake they had to find an opening.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were available on mail or physical it you booked a meeting with the guidance coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: After finally getting to register alle the courses I wished for had an opening.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Double check the language agreement.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a hard schedule to follow. On my first try I had an overlap and therefore had to reschedule subjects. Then I got on a lot of evening classes combined with some morning classes too that meant I was on campus for 12 hours a day two days a week because of the breaks between the courses where too short to to home and come back to uni.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Anthropology once a week from 16-17.30 and again with a work class from 19-20. The level were high as it was a must to remember all theorists and their theories for the exam. During the semester we had to write a project which where 50 % of the end final grade. 
Applied linguistics two times a week from 9-10:30 the level was okay, and the exam was a home assignment that I could write in my native language. 
Latin american literature two times a week from 9-10:30 or 12-13:30 with a working class once a week at 12-13. Quite hard level, had to read a lot of texts which were difficult to understand. the lectures were fast and you had to have good notes in order to understand the course and pass the exam. the work load were high as there was assignments and tests during the semester. 
Gramatica descriptiva once a week from 10:30-12 following a work class from 12-13. Hard level having to learn a lot of rules but we got a lot of time set off to practice in pairs. 
Fundamentos para el uso y el analisis de la lengua española two times a week from 16-17:30 and from 19-20:30 plus a work class once a week from 19-20. This was properly one of the hardest course I could have chosen as the professor said it should not be offered to erasmus as even 50% of the spanish students dont pass. There were a lot of tests during the semester and on the test there were even trick questions which for a erasmus were impossible to know. There were 3 presentations and a group project and you could only add the grade if you had passed the final exam with a high suspensionrate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The professor always presented from a prepared powerpoint. Some of them had made them public for the student to view during the lecture and other after the lecture. The student was expected to write notes but were not asked to participate in the lectures, there were no discussion questions given for the student to discuss the thems.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I adjusted rather quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: open up and show that you are interested in getting to know them. ask them for a shared whatsapp.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: they have lectures till late in the evening. eating dinner late.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: their happy personalities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: they require you to memorise everything which is a lot different from what we are teached. they value memorising over critical discussions in fact they are not interested in your opinion only what the books say you must know. try to socialise as much as you can in the beginning to establish a social group of people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: you need to know spanish as almost no one speaks english anywhere not even at the university

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: knowing what you are capable of doing when being alone or by yourself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: trying to keep up with the spanish students. memorising everything.
